description: Blue mushrooms on a knot of root, lit from inside. Gnarloak carries a whole grove in its shoulders.
lore: It does not go out. Not for wind, not for rain, not for a ford — a knot of root with nine or ten caps burns dim and blue and cold in the hand for four months, and costs thirty gold. [[characters/a6d7323d|Gunnar]] walks nights with one caged in wire on his pack and considers the matter settled.

[[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] will not have one in the house, and puts it plainly. A lamp lets you keep walking. A fire makes you stop, and sit, and put your hands out, and then somebody says a true thing and somebody else is there to hear it. He knows how that sounds coming from an old man. He is an old man. He has also spent forty years selling one road at a fireside, a listening at a time, to keep it firm under somebody's feet, and he does not bring her into the argument. Gunnar, who knows about her, does not either.
gm_notes: Two friends, one disagreement, both right. Wendell's objection is the Keeping stated as an opinion about lamps; the woman on the east road is never named by either of them.
